title: The tawaf of Ifadah

segments.voice: Yesterday, shaving or trimming, and your line: a new start. Did you close one small thing and begin the next one clean? Day one thousand one hundred thirty-six.

The Hajj is nearly over, and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is told that Safiyyah, one of his wives, has started her period. His first question is practical: is she going to hold us up? Will the whole party have to wait for her? Then a second question. Did she already do the tawaf, the circling of the Ka'ba, after the day of sacrifice? Yes, they tell him, she did. Then, he says, let's go. That one question decided whether everyone waited. Today, the tawaf of Ifadah.
screen: `IS SHE GOING TO HOLD US UP?` → `DID SHE ALREADY CIRCLE?` → `THEN LET'S GO.`

segments.voice: First, where it falls. The pilgrims have stood at Arafah, slept at Muzdalifah, thrown the stones, offered the sacrifice and cut their hair. Then they go up to Mecca. Jabir's account in Sahih Muslim says the Prophet rode to the House, circled it, and prayed zuhr in Mecca. Then he came to his own clan as they drew water from Zamzam, and drank. Second, the Qur'an's line for it. In Surah Al-Hajj, after the sacrifice, pilgrims are told to finish their unkempt state, fulfill their vows, and "go around the ancient House." Commentators connect that line to this circling. Third, why it's called essential. Tradition counts it among the pillars of Hajj, the parts without which the Hajj isn't complete. Some other rites, if missed, can be made up with an offering. This one has to be done. That's the weight behind Safiyyah's story. His question suggests the whole party would have waited for it, and when he heard it was done, nothing else stood in the way. Fourth, what it finishes. With this circling, and the walk between Safa and Marwa for those who still owe it, the last restrictions of ihram lift. The pilgrim who arrived at the boundary in two white cloths is now, in the eyes of the law, free. There's another circling still to come, at the very end, but that belongs to a later day. Today's is the one the Hajj stands on. Notice the shape of it. After all the big, open places, the plain, the valley, the pillars, the journey comes back to the same small center it started from, and goes around it again.
screen: `UP TO MECCA, AFTER THE SACRIFICE.` · `GO AROUND THE ANCIENT HOUSE.` · `A PILLAR OF HAJJ.` · `THE LAST OF IHRAM LIFTS.` · then, large: `THEN LET'S GO.`

segments.voice: The practice: finish a thing properly. Settle, and breathe. Think of something you've nearly done. A letter that only needs signing. A repair that only needs one more screw. A conversation that stopped just short of the point. Find the last step, the one that makes it count, the one the whole thing stands on. See yourself doing it, slowly, all the way to the end. If you pray, you can ask for help finishing it. If you don't, just let the finished version sit in your mind. The bell holds the time.
The tawaf of Ifadah. The circling of the Ka'ba after Arafah and the day of sacrifice, a pillar of Hajj that has to be done. Today's word.
Your line: the essential circling. Today, do the last step of that nearly finished thing, the one everything else depends on. Tomorrow: the days of tashriq. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-six.

howItsDone: After the stoning, sacrifice and haircut, pilgrims go to Mecca and circle the Ka'ba in the tawaf of Ifadah, a required pillar of Hajj, often followed by the walk between Safa and Marwa.

notes: Safiyyah's story: Bukhari 1757 (also 1733, 4401; Muslim 1211). Confirm number and the paraphrase of 'is she going to hold us up?'.

Muslim 1218 (Jabir): rode to the House, did ifadah, prayed zuhr in Mecca, came to Banu Abd al-Muttalib at Zamzam and drank. (Ibn Umar's report in Muslim 1308 says he prayed zuhr at Mina; scholars reconcile the two.) Confirm whether a Keeper wants this noted.
Pickthall 22:29 fragment 'go around the ancient House': verify exactly before release.
'Scholars count it among the pillars of Hajj' and 'other rites can be made up for': a general fiqh claim (softened from "every school"), not from the cited texts; confirm or soften.
'The last restrictions of ihram lift' (second tahallul), with sa'y for those who still owe it: confirm.
The farewell tawaf (day 1138) is only mentioned, not taught.
